## Use Cases

- Animated channel content, every week.: Ship channel intros, explainer cuts, and full episodes without scaling your team. Your character keeps the same face from the first thumbnail to the 1,800th frame — viewers actually notice.
- Animated explainers, in lunch breaks: Turn a curriculum unit or course module into a 3-minute cartoon. The same instructor character shows up across every lesson — students recognize the format, retention improves.
- 30-second brand ads, same-day: Brief the AI, lock your mascot, ship a cartoon ad in one afternoon. A/B test variants without re-briefing a vendor.
- Personalized bedtime stories: Type tonight's story; watch the cartoon together 20 minutes later.
- Trailers without a video team: Game trailers, app demos, and agency reels — animated in hours, not weeks.

## How It Works

- Upload your hero's photo: Upload one photo of your character, or describe them in a sentence. We lock the face, outfit, and voice into a saved profile you can reuse forever — across episodes, trailers, and shorts.
- Storyboard your story for free: Paste a script, type a prompt, or have the AI expand a one-line idea into structured scenes. Storyboards render with no watermark on the free tier — iterate as much as you want before spending video credits.
- Stitch into a multi-minute short: Hit Generate. We stitch your scenes via shared first/last frames into a multi-minute short — voiceover, music, and captions baked in. Re-roll any single scene without rebuilding the whole video.

## FAQ Anchors

- [What is an AI animation video generator?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): An AI animation video generator turns a single character photo or a written story into a fully animated video — characters, storyboards, voiceover, and background music — without an animator on staff. You upload a hero photo or paste your story; we lock the character, generate the storyboards (free, no watermark), and stitch the scenes into a multi-minute short you can post anywhere.
- [How do I make an AI animation video from a photo or text prompt?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): Three steps. First, upload a photo of your hero or describe them in a sentence — we lock the face, outfit, and voice into a saved character profile. Second, paste your story or let the AI expand a one-line idea into structured scenes; storyboards render for free with no watermark, so you can iterate before spending any video credits. Third, hit Generate — we stitch the scenes together with voiceover and music.
- [How does this compare to traditional animation studios?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): Studios serve a different need: frame-perfect, bespoke craft for tentpole brand work. We focus on speed and budget for marketing, education, and creator workflows where shipping matters more than pixel-perfect manual control. Many of our customers use both — studios for hero campaigns, us for the everyday content engine that runs every week.
- [How does this compare to other AI animation video tools like AnimateAI?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): Three differences. First, your characters stay on-model across long episodes, not just within a 30-second clip — we stitch scenes via shared first/last frames so the same hero shows up in scene 1 and scene 20. Second, our storyboard tier is free with no watermark, so you can shape the whole story before paying anything. Third, when something goes wrong with a render, real human support replies; credits don't disappear into a queue.
- [What output formats are supported, and can I use the videos commercially?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): Standard MP4 and MOV exports at common social platform resolutions and aspect ratios — vertical for TikTok and Reels, square for Instagram feed, widescreen for YouTube. Stitch multiple scenes for longer episodes. You can use outputs commercially when you have the necessary rights to the prompts, reference images, voices, characters, brands, and source material you provide. Specific resolution caps and durations vary by plan; latest list lives on the pricing page.
- [What rights and safety rules should I follow?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): Only upload photos, voices, logos, characters, and story material you own or have permission to use. AI Animation Video does not guarantee that generated output is cleared for every commercial use, especially if it resembles a real person, public figure, protected character, trademark, or copyrighted style. Do not create deepfakes, political impersonation, sexual content, or unsafe children's content; education and family projects should use original characters and age-appropriate prompts.
- [Can my characters stay consistent across multiple videos?](https://aianimation.video/#faq): Yes. Save a character to your library once — name, face, outfit, voice — and reuse that profile in every future render. The same protagonist appears identical across episodes, trailers, and shorts. We treat character identity as a first-class object, not a per-prompt guess, so the hero in scene 1 stays the hero in scene 1,800 — even when you switch art styles.
